title: 7 Fundamental Concepts of Sales for Beginners
summary: This video breaks down seven fundamental concepts of sales for beginners, covering the difference between sales and marketing, market positioning, cold outreach basics, discovery calls, and managing objections. The creator shares insights from a decade in direct sales to help founders and sales reps understand how to structure their approach effectively.
key_points: Sales is like a fisherman casting directly to catch one specific fish, whereas marketing is setting up the broader environment to attract fish to the right spot.
Your company's position in the market determines your sales approach; do not pretend to be a massive enterprise if you are a small startup.
The primary purpose of a cold call or email is to start a conversation and get the prospect on a meeting, not to pitch your entire company.
A discovery call should focus on understanding the prospect's current situation and problems rather than pitching your product right away.
A complete sales cycle includes milestones such as a Discovery Call, Demo Call, Starting a Free Trial, and Management or Legal/Procurement calls.
Always put a time bound of two to four weeks on a free trial and establish clear success criteria with the prospect.
When handling objections like 'this is too expensive', acknowledge their concern and ask follow-up questions to understand the need behind the need.
content:
The creator breaks sales down into seven fundamental parts for people starting from zero, founders who have never sold, or those looking for their first sales job. He draws on over a decade of direct sales experience and coaching over 5,000 people through HigherLevels.com.

1. The Difference Between Sales and Marketing
- The creator uses a fishing analogy. 'Sales is when your rod has actually been casted, the bait is in the water and a fish has actually eaten the bait.' It is everything done to get individual fish one-on-one and bring them in the boat.
- Marketing is often overlooked when eager founders want to make 1000 cold calls or spam 10,000 emails instead of taking a strategic approach.
- When marketing is dialed in, it is much easier to sell because you have warmed up people and have the correct marketing motion.

2. Your Company's Position in the Market Determines Your Sales Approach
- The creator shares his experience at a 250-person database startup that hired former Oracle employees. When competing against Oracle, the company would claim 'we're the market leader in this, we are world-class, we are best of breed.' 
- The creator claims that when competing against the world's number one company as a smaller startup, it is not realistic to act like you are the world's number one. Instead, you should focus on a handful of use cases where you perform at an exceptionally high level and highlight how large companies waste money on cloud costs or lack monitoring.
- Don't beat your chest and act like a huge well-funded startup disrupting the world if you are a five-person company.

3. Cold Call, Email, And Message Basics
- A marketing email is trying to generate interest to get someone to click or sign up for an event.
- Your job when cold calling or emailing is to start a conversation and get them on a meeting, which generally means 'less is more', short and sweet, and focused on what they are doing today to interact with you.
- Example of a cold call opening: 'Hey John, my name's Eric, I'm the founder of Higher Levels and I just wanted to reach out to you directly because I saw you guys are using AWS. We actually help AWS users reduce their cloud spend by about 20% year over year. I was just curious if that's something you've considered and how you're using your AWS services today.'
- The whole purpose of a sales cold call and email is truly to start a conversation.

4. Discovery Call
- When you get a prospect to agree to a 30-minute phone call to learn more about what you do, it is commonly referred to as a discovery call.
- A common mistake for first-time sellers is getting on the call and spending 12 minutes talking all about themselves without asking a single question about what the prospect is doing.
- A great 30-minute call involves spending the first 18-20 minutes asking questions about what they do today to even see if your solution makes sense.

5. What Is An Entire Sales Cycle In The First Place
- If you're selling business-to-business or technical products, the major milestones to walk your prospect through are:
  1. Discovery Call
  2. Demo Call (Technical deep dive)
  3. Starting a Free Trial (Assuming everyone is on the same page and it is time-based, such as 2 to 4 weeks, with clear success criteria)
  4. Management, Procurement, or Legal calls (to understand purchasing, contracts, and redlining)
- The value of having a structured process is that if a prospect gets a free trial and doesn't make progress for a month, you have the muscle to walk away if they aren't willing to participate or bring others to the call.

6. Handling Objections
- If you haven't made a single cold call or gotten on the phone, don't worry about figuring out how to handle all objections.
- A simple framework for handling an objection like 'this is too expensive' (whether on a cold call or discovery call):
  - Acknowledge what they are saying and ask for the need behind the need: 'Hey, completely understand. Quite frankly, that is something I hear often. People think that we are rather expensive, and maybe that's the case, but often times it's because maybe their need isn't big enough or they don't fully understand what they do.'
  - Give it credit: 'That could be valid. Maybe we are too expensive. Maybe now's not the right time. Why is that? Just tell me a little bit more about that so I fully understand it.'

7. The Mentality of Someone New To Sales
- It is very tempting when you first get started and make 10 great cold calls to think you've mastered cold calling and want to immediately learn emails.
- The creator advises new sellers to double and triple down on what is working until you have fully saturated and milked the one thing you are good at before exploring other channels.
